hypotheses.paper: On ℝ², ≪_U by the chains of timelike segments (t' − t > |x' − x|) inside U; ≤_U by the chains whose steps are causal segments (t' − t ≥ |x' − x|) inside U or rational jumps (t, q) → (t, q'), q < q' in ℚ, {t} × [q, q'] ⊆ U (evidence, roadmap.toml:1055); (i) I±_U(x) Minkowski's, hence open; ≪ ⊆ ≤; transitivity by concatenation
hypotheses.note: Coordinates (t, x) = (p.1, p.2). |Δx| ≤ Δt is written as two coordinate inequalities (RationalJumpCausal :105, strict RationalJumpChronal :109), the jump as IsRationalJump (:113: same t, x increasing, both ends in range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)); every step carries segment ℝ a b ⊆ U, which for a jump is {t} × [q, q'] ⊆ U. ≤_U := TransGen (rationalJumpStep U), ≪_U := TransGen (rationalJumpChronalStep U) (:171). Every field of Causality is discharged: le_refl by a trivial causal step, le_trans/lt_trans by TransGen.trans, monotony by inclusion of segments, le_of_lt step by step (RationalJumpChronal.causal), isOpen_lt_right/left by moving the end of the last chronal step / the start of the first (:143, :153, with eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen of Causal.OneWayMembraneChronal, reused). In coordinates (rationalJumpPlane_le_imp, :234): t and t + x do not decrease along ≤_U, and between two points at the same time ≤_U is equality or a rational jump (the rational line's relation); ≪_U lies in Minkowski's chronology (rationalJumpPlane_lt_imp, :216).

hypotheses.paper: (ii) absolutely minimal on every open set for every cover: a segment, and a jump (the rationals being dense), subdivide into steps each inside one member of the cover (a Lebesgue number of a compact segment), as for the rational line; in either reading (OQ-18)
hypotheses.note: Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W asks both halves, ≤ and ≪, as chains of relations localised in the members V ⊓ O of the cover. transGen_of_segment_subdivision (:293): if R holds between the points of [a, b] at any two rational parameters 0 ≤ c₁ < c₂ ≤ 1, the equal subdivision at k/n with ‖b − a‖/n below a Lebesgue number (lebesgue_number_lemma_of_metric) gives an R-chain whose segments each lie in some V ⊓ O. A sub-segment of a causal (resp. timelike) segment is causal (resp. timelike) at any parameters (RationalJumpCausal.sub :255, RationalJumpChronal.sub :266); a sub-segment of a rational jump at rational parameters is a rational jump (IsRationalJump.sub :277): the rational nodes k/n are what keeps the jump's pieces rational, which is the one point where the plane differs from a model with arc-connectedness. Then rationalJumpPlane_absolutelyMinimalOn (:358) for every open W and every cover, and rationalJumpPlane_absolutelyMinimal (:395) by Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff. No causal curve is used: this is the rational line's route (Causal.rationalLine_absolutelyMinimal, Causal/NestedConverse.lean:303), not cor:causalement_connexe_minimal.

hypotheses.paper: (iii) Chronal neighbours: (t ∓ ε, x) lie in any open set about (t, x). Hence it is tarentin (ChronalNeighbours.tarentin)
hypotheses.note: In a ball of radius ρ about v inside V, (t − ρ/2, x) ≪_V v ≪_V (t + ρ/2, x) by one vertical timelike segment each (:402); Tarentin by Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours.tarentin (:430).

hypotheses.paper: (iv) T = t + x/2 is a time function, strictly increasing along jumps and along non-trivial causal segments. Hence it is causal and has curves_extend

hypotheses.note: rationalJumpStep.eq_or_lt (:436): a causal segment with Δt = 0 is trivial, with Δt > 0 it raises 2t + x by at least Δt; a jump raises it by Δx > 0. Causality.HasTimeFunction (:459), IsCausal by HasTimeFunction.isCausal (:464), CurvesExtend by HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend (in the separation).

hypotheses.note: rationalJumpPlane_le_zero_one (:470): one jump. rationalJumpPlane_causalCurveOn_eq (:478): a causal curve of any open W over any [s₀, s₁] with (γ s₀).1 = (γ s₁).1 is constant; rationalJumpPlane_not_exists_causalCurveOn (:508) and the conjoined rationalJumpPlane_zero_one_separates (:773): no causal curve joins (0, 0) to (0, 1) in any open set over any segment s₀ ≤ s₁. rationalJumpPlane_not_causallyArcConnected (:520), the ladder's Causality.CausallyArcConnected at M. Beyond: no non-empty open set is causally arc-connected (:553, a rational jump in a small ball, exists_rationalJump_chronal :528), so not locally causally arc-connected either (:564).

findings: The evidence's (v) (programme/roadmap.toml:1055) cites 'the rational line's argument, Causal.rationalLine_separates, Causal/RationalLineExtras.lean:289'. That line is the rational line's conjoined ladder witness. hypotheses.note: Causally open in the future and in the past, DEC-8's two-sided form (rationalJumpPlane_causallyOpen, :641). For y ∈ J⁺_U(V) from x ∈ V, the chain moved by −(s, 0) is a chain of U for small s (rationalJumpStep.eventually_shift :604: the step kinds are invariant under time translation, a jump keeps its rational ends, and the moved segment stays in a thickening of the compact segment inside U; rationalJumpPlane_le_eventually_shift :629). Then x − (s, 0) ∈ V, x − (s, 0) ≤_U y − (s, 0) ≪_U y, and I⁺_U(y − (s, 0)) is an open neighbourhood of y inside J⁺_U(V). The past is the same, moving up. Strongly causal in the open form (:687): a small open box in t and t + x, both monotone along ≤, contains the diamonds of its points. Not causally compact (:716): J_M((0, 0), (0, 1)) meets {0} × ℝ in the rationals of (0, 1) and in no irrational point, so it is not closed. Hence not globally hyperbolic.

kb_proposals: pattern — Absolute minimality without arc-connectedness, for a polygonal causality. If every kind of step subdivides at rational parameters into steps of the same kind, Causal.transGen_of_segment_subdivision gives AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for every W and every cover: the equal subdivision at k/n, below a Lebesgue number of the compact segment. Causal and timelike segments subdivide at any parameter, a rational jump only at rational ones. Both halves of AbsolutelyMinimalOn (≤ and ≪) go this way. Causal.rationalJumpPlane is the either-reading witness of chronal_neighbours ⇏ causally_arc_connected: no causal curve joins (0, 0) ≤ (0, 1), by the rational line's intermediate-value argument (T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected).

pattern — Causal openness of a polygonal causality without push-up. If the kinds of step are invariant under a time translation, move the chain by −(s, 0): Causal.rationalJumpStep.eventually_shift keeps the moved segment in U by a thickening of the compact segment. Then add one timelike step to y; J⁺ is open, and J⁻ likewise. Causal.rationalJumpPlane is causally open in the future and in the past, with chronal neighbours, absolutely minimal on every open set, and push-up fails in every non-empty open set. So push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open (Lemma K's route) does not reverse, not even under absolute minimality (Causal.not_locallyPushUp_of_chronalNeighbours_causallyOpen_bare) (T-abs-chronal-not-arc-connected).

notes: One new file, sorry-free and clean under warningAsError, namespace Causal. It graduates unchanged as Causal/RationalJumpPlane.lean (module Causal.RationalJumpPlane). It imports Causal.OneWayMembraneChronal (reused for eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen; its closure is ETT-layer), Causal.Ladder.Rules (causal_ladder, used once, for ¬ CausallyPlain), and Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.Irrational. The planner's sketch holds in every part (i)–(vi); nothing is refuted and the model is the evidence's model unchanged. The delicate point, absolute minimality without arc-connectedness, holds by the rational line's route. Each step subdivides into steps of the same kind inside the members of the cover. For a rational jump the subdivision must be at rational parameters, so it is the equal one at k/n below a Lebesgue number. Both halves of AbsolutelyMinimalOn (≤ and ≪) are discharged, for every open set and every cover. Two small departures from the sketch: the time function is 2t + x, the evidence's t + x/2 doubled; (v) uses the rational line's intermediate-value argument, not the last-parameter one. Beyond the target, the plane is causally open (two-sided) and strongly causal in the open form, and it is not causally compact. Push-up and causal arc-connectedness fail in every non-empty open set. It is thus the ladder's first absolutely minimal, causally open model with chronal neighbours and without push-up (for_keeper.fails_optional). Its time reversal is the image under (t, x) ↦ (−t, −x), argued, and is not stated. No question for the author: the target defines both relations by chains of segments, and the Lean takes that definition.
